subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What default safety policy should OpenClaw enforce for external or plugin-created recurring agentTurn cron jobs that can spend model quota?
rationale: The evidence shows a real source-level risk, but the fix changes compatibility-sensitive cron defaults, plugin scheduling contracts, doctor/update behavior, model-provider policy, and possible quota thresholds.

options.title: Default disabled with operator approval
options.body: Make externally or plugin-created recurring agentTurn jobs inactive until an operator enables them, surface a doctor/update diff, and add explicit model/cost warnings while keeping broader budget work linked to the related issues.

options.title: Keep enabled but warn loudly
options.body: Preserve existing enabled-by-default compatibility and add doctor/status/run warnings for inherited expensive models, accepting that jobs can still run before acknowledgement.

options.title: Defer to scheduling RFC
options.body: Leave this issue open only as input to the broader non-forgeable scheduling API and avoid changing current cron defaults until that design lands.

recommendation.title: Default disabled with operator approval
recommendation.body: Make externally or plugin-created recurring agentTurn jobs inactive until an operator enables them, surface a doctor/update diff, and add explicit model/cost warnings while keeping broader budget work linked to the related issues.

likelyOwner.reason: The current cron implementation history in this checkout points to Vincent Koc across the core files that would need policy-aware changes.
